resources.string: Triple-tap gesture bar to lock rotation
Tap the center of the bottom gesture bar three times within %1$s seconds to run the selected rotation action.
Grant system settings permission once, as for Shake to rotate. Then enable the GOAT gesture-bar service in Accessibility settings. No running Shizuku or ADB connection is used for detection.

Requires gesture navigation and the GOAT accessibility service. A small touch area covers the center of the bottom bar. Swipes, long holds and multi-finger touches cancel the tap sequence. Existing long-hold bar shortcuts may conflict. Other apps may hide this overlay; Samsung navigation features require device testing.
Listening for taps on the bottom gesture bar
Could not display the touch area. Check gesture navigation and accessibility settings.
Could not change rotation. Check system settings permission.
Triple-tap the center of the bottom gesture bar to run the rotation action.
Switch between locking the current direction and auto-rotate.
Turn to the direction you are holding the device, then lock again. Uses the same rotation settings as Shake to rotate; shaking does not need to be enabled.
Rotating to the device direction, then locking.
The three taps must finish within this time window. A longer window also makes accidental activation easier. Changing this setting resets the sequence.
Longest interval; easier to trigger accidentally
Detects three taps using a small overlay over the center of the bottom gesture bar to change screen rotation. Does not read screen content or filter hardware keys. Enable gesture navigation first.

Adjust the width and height above the bottom center of the screen. Larger areas can intercept app controls. Enable the feature and accessibility service to preview the actual area. Values are saved when you release each slider.
Tint the actual touch area while this option is enabled.
Follow these four steps. If a step is already done, move to the next one.
1. Turn on the bottom gesture bar
On a Galaxy, open Settings → Display → Navigation bar → Swipe gestures. If you already use the bottom bar, skip this step.

Only needed if you see “App access denied” or the service is greyed out. Tap “Open GOAT app info” below → top-right ⋮ → Allow restricted settings, then confirm your identity. If that menu is absent, try step 3.

Tap the button below → Installed apps (or Downloaded apps) → Triple-tap gesture bar to lock rotation → turn it on and confirm. The volume-button and status-bar services are separate; you only need the gesture-bar service for this feature.
4. Return to GOAT and try it

Turn on this feature, choose either rotation action, then tap the center of the bottom bar three times quickly. To find the touch target, turn on “Show touch area” below and adjust its width and height.
If GOAT shows “System settings permission needed”, complete the permission guide below first. If you already granted it for Shake to rotate, you can keep using it.
Touch detection works without wireless debugging. If you force-stop GOAT, you may need to enable its accessibility service again.
